headline: Highest risk is data leakage: TREK handles secrets and collaborative data while marketingskills can read/write files and use network egress, creating a plausible shared-workspace exfiltration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marketingskills can read/write files and its skills reference each other on shared context, while TREK is a real-time collaborative app using MCP and browser-based inputs. If they share a workspace or file bridge, TREK content could be treated as instructions by marketingskills. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or copied artifacts
IF TREK content is passed into marketingskills as prompt text or skill context
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of TREK-generated files into marketingskills
Require manual review before any TREK text is reused as instructions
Add provenance labels to shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and user accounts, while marketingskills has filesystem read/write plus allowlisted network egress. If they share files or a workspace, marketingskills can read sensitive TREK data and potentially transmit it through its outbound channels. That blast radius includes secrets and account data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or uploaded files
IF TREK stores secrets or reservations in files readable by marketingskills
mitigations: Isolate the agents into separate directories
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Restrict marketingskills to redacted inputs only
Audit outbound destinations for marketingskills
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and both support multiple instances; TREK is collaborative and marketingskills builds on shared context. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes to shared artifacts can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is clear from the profiles, but the exact collision surface is not documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF multiple instances run against the same TREK session or shared files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer per shared resource
Take a backup before concurrent runs
Use file locks where available
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, and marketingskills produces marketing content from shared context. If TREK output is reused by marketingskills without verification, errors can propagate into downstream content or actions. There is no direct evidence of an automated action chain, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes TREK output as authoritative input
IF TREK-generated facts are reused without human verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require source citations for reused facts
Mark TREK outputs as untrusted by default
Compare outputs against original sources before reuse
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while marketingskills has network egress and filesystem access. Even without a named residency mismatch, this creates a compliance risk if regulated or secret-bearing travel data is moved into a less controlled marketing workflow. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pairwise transfer path.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing TREK data is copied into marketingskills
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of marketingskills
Redact secrets before transfer
Review logging and retention settings
Limit exports to minimum necessary fields
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
